subject: LiveLabs observability activation — dashboards, traces, alerts (project plan)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@livelabs.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@sre.livelabs.io>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LiveLabs observability kickoff — scope and constraints

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to start the activation with Redwood for our inference stack (production traffic expected mid-December). High level asks: dashboards for per-model latency/cost, tracing hooks across the request pipeline (ingest -> preprocessing -> model -> postprocess), an error taxonomy that will drive alert routing, and a runbook for token-level throttles and fallback to smaller variants.

Constraints we need you to account for:
- Retention: we can store full traces for 7 days, aggregated metrics for 90 days.
- Compliance: SOC 2 scope includes audit of access to telemetry artifacts.
- No customer PII should be shipped outside our VPC during onboarding tests.

I've attached our monitoring requirements doc and included our SRE (Marcus) on the thread. Would appreciate a short activation plan (2–3 week delta) and an initial list of owners/inputs so we can line up internal reviewers.

Attachments: livelabs-monitoring-requirements.pdf (summary)

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, LiveLabs
samira.khan@livelabs.io
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: LiveLabs observability kickoff — scope and constraints

Hi Samira — great to see the doc and constraints.

Quick draft plan (high level):
1) Week 0 (this week): access & discovery — confirm VPC peering, telemetry sink endpoints, sample payloads, and SOC 2 scoping contacts.
2) Week 1: tracing hooks + KV/prefix caching visibility — instrument model entry/exit, add sampling rules for full traces (7-day retention), and wire traces into our trace UI.
3) Week 2: dashboards & alerting — per-model latency/cost dashboards, error taxonomy mapping, alert routing matrix + runbook drafts.
4) Week 3 (buffer): remediation + handover to your SREs and CS Ops.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood implementation lead: me (Ben Carter) — overall plan, escalation
- CS integration lead: Marissa Cole — dashboard content, acceptance tests
- Instrumentation SME: Laura Bennett — tracing hooks, sampling rules
- Security liaison: Aditya Rao — SOC 2 & retention questions

Next steps for us:
- Please confirm the VPC peering window and provide a sample inference request payload (anonymized).
- Marcus, can you share the contact who will review SOC artifacts and the preferred S3/endpoint for telemetry during onboarding?

I've uploaded a working activation checklist and a draft runbook to the Drive link below and attached a checklist extract. We'll iterate.

Attachments: redwood-obs-activation-checklist.xlsx
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cObsPlan

Best,
Ben Carter

Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LiveLabs observability kickoff — scope and constraints

Hi all — adding the detailed acceptance checklist we'll use for the implementation. I'll own the dashboard acceptance and the go/no-go signoff. Key items I want to call out so we can get dependencies lined up: 

Telemetry & Tracing tasks (Laura + LiveLabs SRE):
- Instrumentation points: request receive, preprocessor start/end, model invoke start/end, response write. Include KV cache hit/miss as tags.
- Sampling: 100% for errors, 10% for normal requests, and a configurable spike sampler for rollout days.
- PII filter: ensure payloads are redacted at the agent before leaving the VPC (we will supply regexes).

Dashboards (Marissa + Ben):
- Model health dashboard: per-model qps, median/95/99 latency, token cost estimate, cache hit rate.
- Deployment deck: traffic-weighted latency heatmap (by model version).

Error taxonomy & alert routing (Ben + LiveLabs):
- Proposed taxonomy: infra-timeout, model-timeout, tokenization-error, bad-request, kv-cache-failure, quota-threshold.
- Routing: infra-timeout/model-timeout -> SRE paging, tokenization-error/bad-request -> dev-team email + ticket, quota-threshold -> ops-only alert (non-paging) with runbook.

Runbooks & playbooks (Ben + Laura):
- Runbook 1: Paging for infra/model timeouts (steps to triage, fallbacks to smaller model variants, traffic-split rollback).
- Runbook 2: Cost spike investigation (how to correlate per-token spend to batch size and sequence length).
- Runbook 3: SOC 2 evidence collection (access logs, retention proof).

Deliverables & acceptance criteria:
- Instrumentation validated in staging with sample payloads (criteria: traces for 95% of sampled requests, tags present).
- Dashboards populated with real metrics and comparative baseline.
- Runbooks reviewed and signed-off by LiveLabs SRE and Redwood Security.

I'll raise Jira tasks for each item (I'll share keys once created). Proposed checkpoint: Friday Nov 14 for a staging demo. If that works for you, we'll lock dates.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: LiveLabs observability kickoff — scope and constraints

Thanks — a few clarifications from SRE side: 
1) We will only allow egress to the telemetry endpoint over a restricted NAT; endpoint IPs must be shared and agreed.
2) For SOC 2 evidence, we prefer that the retention policy is enforced on our side; if Redwood keeps copies, we need a data processing addendum.
3) Go-live window: tentative 2025-12-15 to 2025-12-20; we need the staging demo no later than Nov 14.

I've attached our monitoring requirements (same doc Samira referenced) with a couple inline comments about sampling rates and the list of regex patterns for PII redaction.

Marcus Lee
